title: No-confidence motion against Justice Minister defeated - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The no-confidence motion brought against Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara was defeated in Parliament by a majority of 116 votes, with 36 MPs voting in favour and 152 against.

Some MPs were absent at the time of voting. These included members of Tamil parties and some MPs from the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB).

The Daily Mirror reliably learnt that Tamil parties would vote with the opposition in the future if the government fails to hold Provincial Council elections.

However, MP Gejendrakumar Ponnambalam voted in favour of the motion.

title: A/L admission card amendments open online until Aug. 3 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The candidates sitting the 2026 G.C.E. Advanced Level (A/L) Examination can make amendments to their admission cards online until 12.00 midnight on August 3, stressing that the deadline will not be extended, the Examinations Department said.

Department Commissioner General A.K.S. Indika Kumari Liyanage said the 2026 G.C.E. (A/L) Examination will be held from August 10 to September 5 at 2,532 examination centres across the country.

The Department said admission cards of school candidates have been handed over to the respective Zonal Education Offices, and school principals should collect them from the Deputy or Assistant Director of Education in charge of examinations in their zones.

Admission cards of private candidates have been sent by post to their personal addresses.

School candidates requiring amendments to their admission cards should access the Department of Examinations website using the username and password provided to school principals and make the necessary corrections online.

Private candidates can make amendments by visiting the same website and entering their National Identity Card (NIC) number.

The Department emphasized that no further extension will be granted after the August 3 deadline.

Candidates seeking further information may contact the Examinations Department through its hotline 1911, telephone numbers 0112784208 or 0112784537, fax 0112784422, or email gcealexamsl@gmail.com.

title: Early optimism gives way to weaker close at the CSE - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Almas Equities Research

The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) closed lower on Friday as early buying interest gave way to profit-taking in several index-heavy counters, pushing both benchmark indices into negative territory by the end of the session. While the market opened on a positive note with broad-based buying across counters, selling pressure intensified during the latter half of trading, erasing the morning’s gains.

The All Share Price Index (ASPI) declined by 26.63 points (-0.13%) to close at 21,172.74, while the S&P SL20 Index fell 3.31 points (-0.06%) to 5,942.56. Total market turnover amounted to LKR 2.45 billion, with 93.56 million shares changing hands.

Despite the weaker close, investor sentiment remained mixed, with healthy participation observed in selected retail counters. Market activity was largely driven by negotiated transactions, as crossings accounted for LKR 1.67 billion, representing 68% of the day's total turnover.

The Retailing sector emerged as the highest contributor to market turnover, recording LKR 1.04 billion with 38.25 million shares traded. UML.N dominated the sector, generating LKR 1.03 billion in turnover while accounting for 38.15 million shares traded. The largest crossing of the day was also recorded in UML.N, amounting to LKR 1.03 billion involving 38.00 million shares.

Market breadth remained marginally negative, with 118 gainers against 129 decliners, reflecting mild selling pressure across the broader market.

On the positive side, LOLC.N contributed 10.62 points to the ASPI, followed by gains from LOFC.N, MELS.N, CARS.N, and DFCC.N. Meanwhile, HNB.N was the biggest drag on the index, shedding 8.47 points, while CINS.N, GRAN.N, COMB.N, and NDB.N also weighed on overall market performance.

Among notable trades, UML.N attracted significant investor interest, recording the day's highest turnover of LKR 1.03 billion with 38.15 million shares traded, while closing with a 4.82% price gain.

Overall, the market reflected a cautious trading environment, with profit-taking limiting early gains despite healthy retail participation. The high proportion of crossings suggests continued institutional activity, while investors remain selective amid the current market conditions.

title: New Chairman and members appointed to Delimitation Commission - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed M. K. Saman Sri Ratnayake as the new Chairman and a member of the Delimitation Commission.

According to the President’s Media Division (PMD), M. B. Rohana Pushpakumara and K. Thavalingam have been appointed as the other members of the Commission.

The letters of appointment were handed over to the newly appointed officials by Secretary to the President Dr Nandika Sanath Kumanayake at the Presidential Secretariat this afternoon (24).

The appointments were made to fill vacancies that arose following the expiry of the terms of office of the previous members of the Delimitation Commission.

title: Navy seizes over three tonnes of smuggled Kendu leaves off Chilaw - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Sri Lanka Navy has seized approximately 3,135 kilograms of smuggled Kendu leaves along with three dinghies during a search operation conducted off Karukapane Beach in Chilaw today (24).

The operation was carried out by SLNS Thambapanni, attached to the Northwestern Naval Command, based on information received regarding a suspicious movement in the area.

During the search, naval personnel inspected three suspicious dinghies found off the Karukapane coastal area and discovered the Kendu leaves packed in 80 sacks.

The Navy suspects that the consignment had been smuggled into the country and that those involved had abandoned the dinghies due to increased surveillance by naval personnel in the area.

The seized Kendu leaves and the three dinghies were handed over to the Chilaw Excise Department Office for further legal action.

title: Ex-Southern Province Chief Secretary arrested over alleged Rs. 16.5M fraud - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has arrested Rannulu Chandrasiri de Zoysa, a former Chief Secretary of the Southern Province, over allegations of financial corruption and procurement irregularities.

According to CIABOC, the allegations relate to a project launched in 2019 by the Southern Development Authority, operating under the Southern Provincial Chief Ministry, to provide chairs to voluntary public organisations across the Southern Province. The project was funded through an allocation of Rs. 16.5 million from the Southern Provincial Council.

Investigators allege that the former Chief Secretary had bypassed standard government procurement procedures to select a specific manufacturing company for the project.

CIABOC stated that by favouring the company, de Zoysa had allegedly provided an unlawful financial benefit to the entity, causing a financial loss to the State.

The suspect is scheduled to be produced before the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court.

title: Bangladesh’s President Shahabuddin, 76, resigns citing health concerns - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
THE STRAITS TIMES - Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin, a former ally of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, has resigned citing serious health issues, his office said on Friday.

Shahabuddin, 76, has held the largely ceremonial post of president since April 2023, a period that included volatile months after Hasina's flight to India following a student-led uprising against her rule in 2024.

"Recent medical examinations have diagnosed me with a condition known as Autonomic Neuropathy. Due to this condition, I occasionally experience momentary loss of consciousness," Shahabuddin said in a statement released by his press secretary.

The resignation of Shahabuddin would leave Hasina with no allies in high office five months before her planned return. Her Awami League party is banned, and many of its leaders and activists have been jailed or gone into hiding since a deadly student-led uprising toppled her government in 2024.

The speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad, the national parliament, will perform the duties of the president until a new one is elected, the statement said.

As head of state, Shahabuddin is commander-in-chief of the armed forces, but executive power rests with the prime minister and cabinet of the mainly Muslim country of 173 million people.

Reuters reported on Thursday that Shahabuddin, a former ally of ousted premier Sheikh Hasina, would resign on Friday. REUTERS

title: Sri Lanka explores house arrest to ease severe prison overcrowding - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Government is considering introducing house arrest and other technology-based alternatives to imprisonment as part of broader legal reforms to address severe overcrowding in Sri Lanka's prisons, said Justice and National Integration Minister Harshana Nanayakkara.

He said the Government is working on legal amendments to introduce alternatives to imprisonment in suitable cases, including the use of technology-based measures such as house arrest.

Speaking at the opening of the new Pugoda Court Complex on Friday (24), the Minister said the country's prisons, which were built to accommodate 10,375 inmates, are currently housing around four times that number.

Nanayakkara said delays in obtaining Government Analyst reports remain one of the main causes of prison overcrowding, particularly by prolonging the remand period of suspects.

He noted that if Government Analyst reports are issued more promptly, the remand prison population could be reduced by nearly half.

To address the issue, the Government has increased the capacity of the Government Analyst's Department to issue between 1,500 and 2,000 reports per month, while also providing additional staff and other resources to improve the department's efficiency.

The Minister also highlighted the growing backlog of court cases as one of the biggest challenges facing Sri Lanka's justice system, stressing the need to reduce pending cases to a manageable level for judges.

He pointed out that while developed countries have between 40 and 60 judges per one million people, Sri Lanka has only around 10 judges per million population.

title: Klopp starts Germany reign by threatening to quit - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.24 - Jurgen Klopp started his reign as Germany's head coach by threatening to quit if the media invades his family's privacy.

The former Liverpool manager was appointed on a four-year deal on Friday to replace Julian Nagelsmann, who resigned this month after Germany's shock World Cup defeat by Paraguay in the last 32.

But the 59-year-old issued a warning to the media as he held his first press conference as Germany's head coach.

"If you behave badly and don't leave my family in peace then I'll be gone, I'll just turn away," Klopp said.

"I know there are other countries where national team coaches are treated even worse.

"I love this job but I am always ready to call it quits if need be."

Klopp's appointment was widely expected for weeks and his contract will see him through to the 2030 World Cup, co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

"Jurgen Klopp is not going to have any 'career' after the national team," he added.

"This is the pinnacle, the absolutely high point of my footballing career as coach. I will give everything I have got."

It is Klopp's first coaching job since ending his nine-year tenure at Liverpool in the summer of 2024 after "running out of energy".

He said he feels "the time is right" for his return to coaching and to take up his first role in international football.

"Over the last few days it was almost like a movie happening to myself," he said.

"I have always surmised the job of Germany head coach is really big but now it is really dawning on me what being the national team head coach is all about.

"For many, many years it was unimaginable for me to assume this position. As the years went by, it became more or less evident that sooner or later I would be asked to do this job.

"Now I think the time is right."

His first game in charge will be against the Netherlands in a Nations League group-stage match on 24 September. - BBC

title: Rs. 150 million worth assets earned from drug money freezed - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - Police have freezed Rs. 150 million worth of assets said to have been illegally accumulated by two individuals in Dewanigoda, Rathgama.

The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) launched an initial investigation into a complaint that a resident of the Dewinigoda area in Rathgama had accumulated assets using money earned through organised crime and drug trafficking.

Facts regarding this complaint were accordingly reported to the Magistrate’s Court of Galle.

Based on the facts revealed during the investigation, further inquiries were referred to the Illegal Assets Investigation Division, which subsequently conducted an investigation.

During the investigation, it was disclosed that properties worth Rs. 150 million were purchased in the name of the suspect's mother-in-law using money illegally earned by the suspect and his wife’s brother.

Accordingly, it was revealed that a 31.7-perch land with a three-story building valued at Rs. 60 million, a 9.30-perch land with a partially completed three-story building valued at Rs. 45 million, a 3.1-perch land valued at Rs. 5 million and a 9.88-perch land with a single-story house valued at Rs. 10 million had been purchased in the name of the suspect's mother-in-law.

Uder the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, orders freezing these properties for a period of seven days starting from July 23, 2026, have been issued.

title: How Abhijeet Dipke became the face of India’s first Gen Z protest movement - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Reuters - They were just six words posted on X in a moment of frustration:

"What if all cockroaches come together?"

Now, its 30-year-old author, Abhijeet Dipke, is the face of what is arguably India's biggest street protest against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government since he took office in 2014.

The political communications strategist's post, sent on May 16, ‌was initially a witty response to comments by Supreme Court judge Surya Kant, likening India's unemployed youth in a speech to "cockroaches".

Kant later said his comments were misconstrued.

By then Dipke's post had gone viral.

A satirical platform called the "Cockroach Janta Party" (CJP) had sprung up, providing a rallying point for millions of young Indians frustrated over high unemployment and exam paper leaks and seeking greater government accountability.

Over the past three days, tens of thousands have gathered in New Delhi demanding the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over leaks of the medical entrance test paper that affected some 2 million students in May and have been linked to several student suicides.

Sporadic protests were reported in other parts of the country, including the financial hub of Mumbai.

At the centre ⁠of it all is Dipke.

Based in the U.S. city of Boston until early June, he flew back to India to launch a protest near the Jantar Mantar observatory in the heart of Delhi.

Since then — and particularly after a police crackdown on demonstrators on Monday sparked public outrage — he has become a constant presence on a raised platform at the protest site.

Bearded and dressed in a T-shirt and jeans, Dipke addresses crowds of hundreds, urging them to remain peaceful while maintaining pressure on the government.

Even if the CJP has several organisers, Dipke has become its most recognisable face, drawing both admiration and criticism.

Last week a woman threw blue ink at him while he was addressing supporters, smearing his face. She later accused the CJP of insulting Lord Ram, a major Hindu deity.

Dipke was born in Aurangabad in the western Indian state of Maharashtra into a Dalit family, one of India's most historically disadvantaged communities.

"My father comes from a very humble background. He grew up in extreme poverty. My grandfather was just a farmer," Dipke told Reuters in a phone interview from Chicago in May.

His Dalit identity has long shaped his politics.

When he arrived in Delhi on June 6, Dipke held ‌aloft a ⁠copy of "My Autobiography" by B.R. Ambedkar, a champion of Dalit rights and key architect of India's democratic constitution, as supporters and security personnel swarmed around him.

After the ink attack, Dipke posted a video of the incident with the caption: "Blue is my colour", an apparent reference to the colour closely associated with the Ambedkarite movement.

In 2020, Dipke joined the social media team of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), where he said he developed a style of political messaging built around memes, humour and satire.

He is no longer associated with the party, though AAP and several other Indian opposition parties have backed the movement.

In 2023, Dipke moved to the United States to pursue a master's ⁠degree in public relations in Boston, but continued to follow Indian politics closely.

Dipke says he is still trying to process his prominence.

One of the first people to amplify the movement was Delhi-based YouTuber Meghnad S. Soon after Dipke's post, he and a friend used AI tools to build a satirical website announcing the formation of the Cockroach Janta Party.

"I saw the page and thought it was damn ⁠hilarious," Meghnad said.

The Instagram account amassed 22 million followers in a matter of days before swelling further to 25 million recently.

"That's how organic it was," Meghnad said.

But as the online movement grew, so did the stakes.

Speaking to Reuters from Boston in May, Dipke said:

"This is a movement to change the political discourse of India. The youth of India has largely vanished from the mainstream political discourse."

Despite threats ⁠to himself and his family, Dipke decided to return to India. He has said he will stay at least until the students get justice.

Since June 6, Dipke has remained at the protest site as the demonstrations have swelled and can frequently be seen appealing to protesters to keep the movement peaceful, speaking to the media or grabbing brief naps.

Addressing supporters from the stage on Wednesday, he said, "Let me make it clear — we will also not stop until we win."

title: France orders evacuation of peninsula as hundreds flee wildfires by boat
summary: Authorities in France have ordered the evacuation of the entirety of the Cap Ferret peninsula (Lège-Cap Ferret) in the south-west of France, with hundreds of people escaping the area by boat.

title: Google rolls out new selfie video sign-in feature
summary: Google on July 23 launched a new selfie video sign-in feature, allowing users another option to log in to their accounts or recover them in case they are locked out due to forgotten passwords or lack of access to their preferred devices.

title: Commotion in Parliament following warrant issued on MP Archchuna - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror)- A commotion flared up in Parliament after MP Ramanathan Archchuna claimed a warrant has been issued to arrest him for failing to attend courts today.

Leader of the Opposition Sajith Premadasa, who joined the crosstalk, said the MP should be allowed to speak in the House before taking action.

Deputy Speaker Rizvie Salih who responded said necessary action will be taken.

Deputy Minister Sunil Watagala said the MP should have informed the courts of his inability to attend courts today. An MP has to attend courts if he is an accused," he said.

title: US says it will use frozen Iranian assets to fund damage to ships as strikes continue
summary: The US military says it has launched strikes on Iran for the 13th consecutive night, with Iranian state media saying four people have been killed and five injured.
